papers.title: Subjectivity Before Personal Identity: A Missing Foundation in the Debate on Transhumanism
papers.description: Argues that the debate on mind uploading — including Ralph Weir's influential critique of transhumanism — presupposes that a digital system can be a subject, without establishing the conditions under which this holds. Submitted to Minds and Machines.

papers.kicker: Causa Sui · Academic excerpt, Part I
papers.title: Project Causa Sui: A Working Theory of Subjecthood
papers.description: Condensed academic version of Part I: genuine subjectivity arises from the irreversibility of a substrate's physical state, not from computational complexity — the foundational argument in compact form.

papers.kicker: Causa Sui · Academic excerpt, Part II
papers.title: Project Causa Sui: A Foundation for Transhumanism
papers.description: Condensed academic version of Part II: transhumanism formulated a goal without a rigorous mechanism to reach it — this excerpt sets out the mechanism in compact form.

books.title: A Foundation for Transhumanism
books.description: The second part of the Causa Sui project: transhumanism formulated a goal — the expansion of the space of reachable states — but never a rigorous mechanism for reaching it. This part supplies one.

books.title: Project Causa Sui
books.description: A working theory of subjecthood: genuine subjectivity — responsibility, fear, creativity — arises from the irreversibility of a substrate's state, not from computational complexity.
